questions.question:
Performance of 1800 students in grades has been shown in the following pie chart.

In which two grades taken together is the number of students 54 less than the number of students in grades B and E taken together?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51d918a1e340828d65d082e104a16c9c16eec5e87d895549d1ddf6f6fc8dd10b.png]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The performance of 1800 students in grades has been shown in the following pie chart.

**Calculation:**

Total percentage of grades B and E = 27% + 8% = 35%

Here, (54/1800) × 100 = 3%

Then, 54 students of 1800 is 3% students

We have to find the sum of two groups in which the sum of percentage = 35% - 3% = 32%

The percentage of students in Grade C = 24%

The percentage of students in Grade E = 8%

The total percentage of Grade C and E = 24% + 8% = 32%

**∴ The number of students is 54 less than the number of students in grades B and E taken together in Grade C and E**

questions.question: A person sold an article at a loss of 18%. Had he sold it for ₹960 more, he would have gained 12%. If the article is sold for ₹3,840, then how much is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The initial loss = 18%

**Formula used:**

S.P. = (Profit/C.P.) × 100

Where, S.P. = Selling price; C.P. = Cost price

**Calculation:**

Let, the cost price of the article = ₹ x

So, (82x/100) + 960 = (112x/100)

⇒ (112x/100) - (82x/100) = 960

⇒ (30x/100) = 960

⇒ x = (960 × 100)/30 = 3200

∴ The cost price of the article = ₹ 3200

Required selling price = ₹ 3840

Then, profit = 3840 - 3200 = ₹ 640

The profit percentage = (640/3200) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The profit percentage is 20%**

questions.question: Two circles touch each other externally at T. RS is a direct common tangent to the two circles touching the circles at P and Q. ∠TPQ = 42°. ∠PQT (in degrees) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠TPQ = 42°

**Concept used:**

The sum of all three angles of a triangle = 180°

The sum of all angles on a straight line = 180°

**Calculation:**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e5e7806c2e7699506c1da9551fd022b9fc6f681405b47b2224853247eda2e622.png] **

Draw a tangent to the circles at T, intersecting QP

So, OT and OQ are two tangents to a common circle from the same external point O

Therefore, OQ = OT then ∠OQT = ∠OTQ

Also, OT and OP are two tangents to a common circle from the same external point O

Therefore, OP = OT then ∠OPT = ∠OTP

∠TPQ = 42°

Then, ∠TPQ = ∠OPT = ∠OTP = 42°

In ΔOPT, ∠OPT + ∠OTP + ∠POT = 180°

⇒ 42° + 42° + ∠POT = 180°

⇒ ∠POT = 180° - 42° - 42° = 96°

Also, ∠POT + ∠QOT = 180°

⇒ 96° + ∠QOT = 180°

⇒ ∠QOT = 180° - 96° = 84°

In ΔQOT, ∠OQT + ∠OTQ + ∠QOT = 180°

⇒ ∠OQT + ∠OQT + 84° = 180° [∵ ∠OQT = ∠OTQ]

⇒ 2 ∠OQT = 180° - 84°

⇒ 2 ∠PQT = 96°

⇒ ∠PQT = 96°/2 = 48°

**∴ The value of ∠PQT (in degrees) is 48°**

questions.question: A boatman can row his boat in still water at a speed of 9 km/h. He can also row 44 km downstream and 35 km upstream in 9 hours. How much time (in hours) will he take to row 33 km downstream and 28 km upstream?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The speed of the boat in still water = 9 km/h

Concept used:

If the speed of a boat in still water is x km/h and the speed of the stream is y km/h, then

Downstream speed = (x + y) km/h

Upstream speed = (x - y) km/h

Time = Distance/Speed

**Calculation:**

Let, the speed of the water = x km/h

Time to cover 44 km downstream = 44/(9 + x)

Time to cover 35 km upstream = 35/(9 - x)

so, [44/(9 + x)] + [35/(9 - x)] = 9

⇒ (44(9-x)+35(9+x))/(81-x²)=9

⇒ 396 - 44x + 315 + 35x = 729 - 9x²

⇒ 9x2 - 9x - 18 = 0

⇒ x2 - x - 2 = 0

⇒ x2 - 2x + x - 2 = 0

⇒ x (x - 2) + 1 (x - 2) = 0

⇒ (x + 1) (x - 2) = 0

⇒ x + 1 = 0 ⇒ x = - 1 ["-" is neglacted]

⇒ x - 2 = 0 ⇒ x = 2

∴ The speed of the water = 2 km/h

So, time is taken to row 33 km downstream and 28 km upstream = [33/(9 + 2)] + [28/(9 - 2)]

= (33/11) + (28/7)

= 3 + 4 = 7 hours

**∴ The boatman will take 7 hours to row 33 km downstream and 28 km upstream**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Here we can see that, 

The Downstream distance in both cases (44 km & 33 km) are divisible by 11

The Upstream distance in both cases (35 km & 28 km) are divisible by 7.

We can say that because the time required (Number of hours) is a complete number in both cases. (9 hrs & all options are complete numbers not in decimal)

Here, according to the question, 

x = 9 km/hr.

⇒ 44/(9 + y) + 35/(9 - y) = 9 hrs

Put y = 2, so that 9 + y will be 11 & 9 - y = 7

⇒ 44/11 + 35/7 = 4 + 5 = 9

y = 2 satisfies the given equation,

Now, 

⇒ 33/(9 + y) + 28/(9 - y) = 33/(9 + 2) + 28/(9 - 2) 

⇒ 33/11 + 28/7 = 3 + 4 = 7 hrs

∴ The boatman will take 7 hours to row 33 km downstream and 28 km upstream

**Given:**

∠CAB = 42° and ∠ABD = 57°

**Concept used:**

The diameter of a circle makes an angle of 90 degree on the circumference

The opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary which means that the sum of either pair of opposite angles is equal to 180 degrees.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e5204045f62ef5d470a1c548a80de254ab32d503de824e4d34ce5b384873e37.png] 

∠ACB = 90° [∵ AB is diameter]

So, in ΔACB

∠CBA = 180° - ∠ACB - ∠CAB

⇒ ∠CBA = 180° - 90° - 42°

⇒ ∠CBA = 48°

So,

∠CBD = ∠CBA + ∠ABD

⇒ ∠CBD = 48° + 57°

⇒ ∠CBD = 105°

Again,

ADBC is a cyclic qudrialteral 

So, ∠CAD = 180° - ∠CBD

⇒ ∠CAD = 180° - 105°

∠CAD = 75°

Difference = 105° - 75°

⇒ 30°

**∴ The difference (in degrees) between the measures of ∠CAD and ∠CBD is 30°**

questions.question: In Δ LMN, the bisector of ∠L and ∠N intersect at an angle of 112°. What is the measure (in degree) of ∠M?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The bisector of ∠L and ∠N intersect at an angle = 112°

**Calculation:**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/77162650fdf0fd39f57301348e02a1ea6ded3c3ab543523607862a1f843abf60.png] **

In ΔLMN, ON is the bisector of ∠N and OL is the bisector of ∠L

∠NOL = 112°

So, ∠NOL = 90° + ∠M/2

⇒ 112° = 90° + ∠M/2

⇒ ∠M/2 = 112° - 90°

⇒ ∠M/2 = 22°

⇒ ∠M = 2 × 22° = 44°

**∴ The value of ∠M is 44°**
